definition: Supporting ODPR workflow unit used by delivery flows, agent discovery flows, and trigger-based flows. It declares metadata, recipe version, type, optional scope, execution policy, intent, instructions, grounding, context format policy, inputs, outputs, steps, gates, review expectations, and lightweight run policy.
doUseFor: Declaring reusable workflow units for delivery flows
Making SDK automation inspectable
Describing CI, release, localization, hybrid, or agent-safe workflows
Using human-authored intent and instructions to guide agent-assisted execution
Using groundingTo to declare the controlled graph node and edge types that ground the work
Using recipe.scope: data-product for workflows that generate, validate, or review DataProductRecipe handoff artifacts
Using one portable document for validation, dry-run, execution, or resume
doNotUseFor: Replacing ODPR's composite flow concepts
Defining data product metadata
Defining catalog object models
Defining graph nodes or edges
Storing provider secrets
Inventing ProductRecipe as a separate root kind
Storing SDK invocation mode, dry-run responses, run manifests, logs, readiness checks, or write-scope results

definition: Supporting ODPR runtime generation configuration document that standardizes SDK-compatible provider profile maps, model defaults, generation paths, portfolio intake policy, and API-key environment variable names.
doUseFor: Standardizing runtime profiles referenced by recipes
Declaring SDK-compatible model and provider defaults
Keeping runtime configuration portable across SDKs, CI/CD systems, MCP servers, and platforms
Resolving runtimeRef fragments against runtimeProfile.providers
doNotUseFor: Embedding raw API keys or secrets
Replacing runtime credential stores
Defining arbitrary provider-specific APIs
Recording provider readiness checks

definition: Supporting ODPR metadata-only discovery document that lists available recipes, optionally organizes entries into catalog groups, and points to complete Recipe files.
doUseFor: Discovering available recipes
Versioning the catalog artifact separately from the ODPR specification version
Organizing recipe entries with optional recipeCatalog.groups and groupRef
Indexing recipe metadata for agents and SDKs
Pointing to complete Recipe files before loading and validating them
doNotUseFor: Embedding full recipe step bodies
Storing credentials
Storing runtime status, planned writes, run ids, logs, provider readiness, or write-scope checks

definition: Primary ODPR handoff document used by product handoff flows. It indexes reviewable files for developers and AI agents implementing one data product.
doUseFor: Indexing Markdown-heavy data product delivery handoff work
Validating mandatory Data Product Recipe sections with stable section IDs
Giving AI agents and developers a predictable data product recipe map
Recording readiness confidence from 0 to 100 and review status
Recording optional recipeRef provenance without requiring workflow execution
doNotUseFor: Requiring developers or AI agents to execute an ODPR workflow recipe
Replacing the ODPS product specification
Embedding full Markdown section bodies in the manifest
Using the non-standard ProductRecipe root kind
Recording SDK run logs, run ids, or execution traces

definition: Composite ODPR flow pattern where an AI agent investigates bounded data product, catalog, graph, or portfolio context to produce grounded answers, findings, impact explanations, or review recommendations.
doUseFor: Declaring bounded AI-agent investigations over retrieved or declared context
Separating evidence-seeking answer generation from artifact delivery flows
Using discoveryType to label standardized discovery step purposes
Using groundingTo to keep answers tied to declared graph node and edge types
Using iterationLimit and exitWhen to stop bounded in-step agent refinement
Producing grounded findings or review recommendations for human review
doNotUseFor: Defining open-ended autonomous agents
Storing hidden prompts, chain-of-thought, memory stores, runtime traces, or tool-loop internals
Replacing trigger-based flows that decide when work becomes applicable
Replacing delivery flows that primarily produce, validate, localize, render, or publish artifacts

definition: One declared operation or standardized agent discovery task in an ODPR recipe.
doUseFor: Ordering SDK or platform operations
Declaring command-specific parameters directly on executable steps
Using discoveryType instead of command for standardized agent discovery steps
Using step intent to explain why an operation exists and what result it should support
Using step instructions to guide agent-assisted interpretation or execution
Using iterationLimit and exitWhen to bound in-step agent or LLM refinement
Overriding runtime references for one LLM-backed operation
doNotUseFor: Arbitrary shell scripting
Using command on a step that declares discoveryType
Hidden side effects
Runtime profile secret storage
General-purpose agent loop languages, loop traces, or internal planning records
Reusable step fragments through uses/template/from/when/foreach/matrix in v1

definition: Workflow intent that declares whether a recipe expects local, hosted, hybrid, or model-free execution.
doUseFor: Separating development from production execution
Declaring local, hosted, hybrid, or none execution expectation
Referencing a default runtime profile for LLM-backed steps
doNotUseFor: Selecting SDK invocation mode such as validate, dry-run, execute, or resume
Registering runtime credentials
Defining model APIs
Replacing SDK runtime configuration

definition: Policy for preferred workflow context serialization such as YAML, TOON, GCF, or automatic fallback.
doUseFor: Declaring compact context serialization preferences
Preferring GCF or TOON sidecars when available
Making prompt and review context representation explicit
doNotUseFor: Changing canonical artifact formats
Embedding full document bodies in recipes
Defining which graph context should be retrieved

definition: Optional ODPR Recipe trigger contract that declares which ODPG graph change pattern can make a recipe applicable.
doUseFor: Declaring graph-triggered recipes as normal Recipe documents
Matching ODPG node and edge additions, removals, or explicit attribute changes
Using controlled node types or * for subject.nodeType
Keeping attribute names explicit in trigger subjects
Pairing trigger patterns with graphContext depth for graph-aware workflow steps
doNotUseFor: Defining ODPG graph nodes or edges
Binding workflow logic to one node id as the default pattern
Using wildcard attribute names
Replacing schedulers, event engines, graph query languages, run logs, or approval records
Embedding full workflow definitions in ODPG

definition: Validation, quality, review, or publication condition that must be visible to recipe runners and agents.
doUseFor: Declaring validation requirements
Making human review explicit
Representing CI or release checks
doNotUseFor: Replacing schema validation
Storing approval records, signatures, workflow pauses, or gate runtime status
Silently approving generated artifacts
